questions.title: Benzathine penicillin prophylaxes against Strep haemolyticus
questions.question: The best effective prophylactic drug in streptococcus haemolyticus is:

explanations.A: Correct. Benzathine penicillin, a long-acting depot form of penicillin G, is the best prophylactic drug against Streptococcus haemolyticus (group A beta-haemolytic streptococcus), maintaining protective drug levels for weeks with a single injection -- the basis for long-term rheumatic fever prophylaxis. Doxycycline, flucloxacillin and ceftriaxone are not the standard prophylactic choice for this organism.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Doxycycline is not the standard long-term prophylactic choice against group A streptococcus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Flucloxacillin, a short-acting oral penicillinase-resistant penicillin, is not suited to long-term depot prophylaxis the way benzathine penicillin is.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ceftriaxone is not the standard long-term prophylactic choice against group A streptococcus.

questions.learning_objective: State that benzathine penicillin is the best prophylactic drug against Streptococcus haemolyticus, owing to its long-acting depot formulation.

questions.title: Sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor
questions.question: Pick out the β-lactamase inhibitor for co-administration with penicillins:

explanations.A: Correct. Sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor, co-administered with a penicillin (as in ampicillin/sulbactam) to protect the antibiotic from bacterial beta-lactamase inactivation and restore its activity against beta-lactamase-producing organisms. Ethacrynic acid, monobactam and moxalactam are not beta-lactamase inhibitors.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ethacrynic acid is a loop diuretic, unrelated to beta-lactamase inhibition.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Monobactam names a distinct beta-lactam antibiotic class (e.g. aztreonam), not a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Moxalactam is a cephalosporin-class antibiotic itself, not a beta-lactamase inhibitor.

questions.learning_objective: Identify sulbactam as a beta-lactamase inhibitor used to protect a co-administered penicillin from bacterial beta-lactamase inactivation.

questions.title: Beta-lactam resistance arises from multiple mechanisms
questions.question: Resistance to Penicillin and other β-lactams is due to:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Beta-lactamase inactivation is a genuine mechanism, but not the only one; it is one of several that together give the complete answer.
explanations.B: Correct. Bacteria can resist penicillin and other beta-lactam antibiotics through several distinct, non-mutually-exclusive mechanisms: inactivation by beta-lactamase enzymes, altered porin structure reducing drug entry into gram-negative organisms, and altered penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) reducing the drug's target affinity. Because all three mechanisms genuinely contribute to beta-lactam resistance, "all of the above" is the correct, most complete answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Altered porin structure is a genuine mechanism, but not the only one; it is one of several that together give the complete answer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Altered PBPs is a genuine mechanism, but not the only one; it is one of several that together give the complete answer.

questions.learning_objective: State that resistance to penicillin and other beta-lactams can arise from beta-lactamase inactivation, altered porin structure and altered PBPs together, not from any single mechanism alone.
questions.module_subject: AUN-MPT-104 > Pharmacology > Introduction to Antimicrobial therapy

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: All of the above"

questions.title: Oral, not IV, vancomycin treats pseudomembranous colitis
questions.question: Concerning vancomycin, the following is correct EXCEPT:

options.A: It is used intravenously in the treatment of pseudomembranous colitis
options.B: It inhibits synthesis of bacterial cell wall.
options.C: Histamine release is one of its adverse effects
options.D: It is effective as a first choice drug in the treatment of MRSA

explanations.A: Correct (as the EXCEPT). Vancomycin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, causes histamine release (red man syndrome) as an adverse effect, and is a first-choice drug for MRSA -- but for pseudomembranous colitis, typically Clostridioides difficile, it must be given orally, not intravenously, since intravenous vancomycin does not reach an effective concentration within the gut lumen where the infection occurs. Oral vancomycin acts locally within the colon instead, so the statement that it is used intravenously for pseudomembranous colitis is the incorrect one, the EXCEPT this question asks for.
explanations.B: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Vancomycin does inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis.
explanations.C: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Histamine release (red man syndrome) is a recognised vancomycin adverse effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Vancomycin is a first-choice drug for MRSA.

questions.learning_objective: State that vancomycin's use in pseudomembranous colitis requires the oral route, not the intravenous route, since only oral dosing reaches an effective luminal gut concentration.
questions.module_subject: AUN-MPT-104 > Pharmacology > Introduction to Antimicrobial therapy

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It is used intravenously in the treatment of pseudomembranous colitis"

questions.title: Ampicillin's characteristic adverse effect is a maculopapular rash
questions.question: A characteristic adverse effect associated with the use of Ampicillin is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Acute haemolytic anemia is not ampicillin's characteristic adverse effect; it is more associated with drugs such as certain sulfonamides in G6PD deficiency.
explanations.B: Correct. A maculopapular (morbilliform) skin rash is a characteristic adverse effect of ampicillin, occurring in a substantial minority of patients and especially common, and non-allergic in mechanism, when ampicillin is given during infectious mononucleosis (EBV infection). This is distinct from acute haemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis or phototoxicity, none of which is ampicillin's characteristic reaction.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Agranulocytosis is not ampicillin's characteristic adverse effect; it is more associated with drugs such as clozapine or certain antithyroid agents.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Phototoxicity is not ampicillin's characteristic adverse effect; it is more associated with drugs such as tetracyclines or fluoroquinolones.

questions.learning_objective: State that a maculopapular rash, not acute haemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis or phototoxicity, is ampicillin's characteristic adverse effect.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Maculpapular rash"

questions.title: Erythromycin for penicillin-allergic Strep pneumoniae infection
questions.question: A patient with hypersensitivity to pencillin V acquired an infection with streptococcus pneumonia, which of the following antimicrobials would be the best choice for that patient?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Amoxicillin/clavulanate is itself a penicillin, which a patient with true penicillin hypersensitivity should avoid.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ampicillin is itself a penicillin, which a patient with true penicillin hypersensitivity should avoid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cefaclor, a cephalosporin, carries some cross-reactivity risk with penicillin allergy and is not the safest choice here.
explanations.D: Correct. In a patient with true hypersensitivity to penicillin V who develops a Streptococcus pneumoniae infection, erythromycin, a macrolide, is the appropriate alternative, since it belongs to a structurally unrelated antibiotic class with no cross-reactivity risk. This is unlike amoxicillin/clavulanate and ampicillin, both penicillins, or cefaclor, a cephalosporin, which carries some cross-reactivity risk with penicillin allergy.

questions.learning_objective: Select erythromycin as the appropriate antibiotic for a penicillin-allergic patient with a Streptococcus pneumoniae infection, avoiding amoxicillin/clavulanate, ampicillin and cefaclor.

questions.title: Ceftriaxone is bactericidal
questions.question: One of the following about ceftriaxone is correct:

options.A: It is effective orally and parenterally
options.B: It acts by inhibiting protein synthesis
options.D: Hepatic toxicity is a main side effect

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ceftriaxone is not orally bioavailable; it requires parenteral (IV or IM) administration only.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ceftriaxone inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, not protein synthesis.
explanations.C: Correct. Ceftriaxone, a third-generation cephalosporin, is bactericidal, inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis and killing susceptible bacteria outright. It is not effective orally, requiring parenteral administration only, and hepatic toxicity is not its main recognised side effect; biliary sludging is the more specific, better-known concern.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hepatic toxicity is not ceftriaxone's main recognised side effect; biliary sludging is the more specific, better-known concern.

questions.learning_objective: State that ceftriaxone is bactericidal, via cell wall synthesis inhibition, and reject the claims that it is orally effective, acts by inhibiting protein synthesis, or causes hepatic toxicity as its main side effect.
questions.module_subject: AUN-MPT-104 > Pharmacology > Introduction to Antimicrobial therapy

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It is bactericidal"
